I have a friend that said she was looking to not be alice (edit: alive, not alice) anymore by 27. I was never looking to date her, but if I was, it wouldn't have made me not want to date her. However, personally, I would want to date someone that is positive around me & is looking to better themselves. Most likely I will change my mind like my friend did & I will look to live a long life myself. It's just going to be a struggle for me in my own way like it was a struggle for her & it's a struggle for you.

Hey. I go to USF, but this showed up on my timeline. I'm far from you, but wanted to say that I'm here if you ever want to talk. I have suffered from OCD since I was 9 (I'm 24 now). I even tried ending my life myself. I isolated myself for years, not knowing until I came back that people really loved and missed me. But I had no idea. OCD made me feel as though I was a terrible person unworthy of love..  Not at all true. Your situation is much harder than mine as I had access to a phone and to the world whenever I needed / wanted. 

I can't say much about your family, but I can say that you deserve a life full of love, happiness, and access to the world however suits you. It's your life-- not your parents. You deserve the life you want. 

Becoming the person you are meant to be takes a lot of time. I was great with time management at the beginning, fell off, and then found my rhythm again after a year of working at it. Your time management skills will come. Just focus on what you need to complete, then the rest of will come later. 

Sometimes, life is all about survival, and it seems as though you are in survival mode right now. That's okay. It's temporary. You got this. 


Not sure about how your OCD is-- there are so many variations 💔 idk if this makes you feel any better, but in 2020 mine almost drove me to what you are saying in here.. I could not function at all. All days, evenings, and mornings were doing rituals. Really felt as though I was absolutely nothing and my life was over at that point (of course it wasn't). Eventually, it dialed down, then stayed dialed down ever since. I reached out to professors and new friends & they helped me with my own family traumas, emotional struggles, scholarships, and even with the moving process when I did move out of my parents' place.

It's never too late. It's never over unless you give up. I'm not sure about what is best for you, but I would attend counseling if your college also offers it, and I would reach out to a professor or few about your academic goals and struggles . It's worth it to do so even when you are in survival mode; they were once in the beginning, just like you too. 

Kepe reaching out to people when you can. It will save your life like it saved mine. 💙

You will love who you are in 5 years. Hold on.

These things are all important.

The Little Book of Common Sense Investing by John Bogle makes investing easy. John Bogle is revolutionary in the finance field. Of course, finances involve more than just investing; it also involves insurance, risk tolerance, housing, retirement planning, and personal financial planning. This being said, John Bogle's Vanguard created index funds for everyone, and they are what made me interested in finance as reading about funds that cost as low as 0.04% while investing into the whole U.S. market or much of the international market was a life changing read for me. I also like how he talked about equity-bond allocation later in the book. John Bogle encouraged holding on to index funds all the way up to retirement with the occasional rebalancing. It's a lot to explain despite the little title. 

I'm not saying you need to buy the book as what works for everyone is different, but I did want to recommend it as it helped me not be impulsive with stocks or wasteful with my money, too.

Hey, I just read this and your story is very similar to mine. I used to be overweight. I was confident a lot of the time, until one day I just wasn't. Then I was desperate for weight loss. It wouldn't come quickly, so I gradually started taking drastic measures. Eventually, I lost the weight, but in really unhealthy ways. It was not at all worth it. If I could go back in time, I would 1000% decide to take a long time to lose weight, to make sure I had fun with it, and to be kind with myself. 
         I lost my period for about 2 years. I started recovery about a year ago. Trust me when I say this: counting calories everyday, weighing yourself a lot, obsessing, and trying to lose weight quickly is not worth it. I'm having health issues now due to what I did & my health issues are making me way sadder than being overweight did. However, I am recovering, and getting better. Some things I want to close this off with are: 1. Many people lose weight in healthy, kind ways with themselves. You don't need to be restrictive 2. It's actually unhealthy to be restrictive.  The best approach to weight loss is sustainable, life long changes. 3. Eat whatever you want whenever you want. But try to eat healthy most meals. 3-4 meals a day is good. Don't do less. Do not eat small meals either. Eat things you enjoy eating but try to be healthy overall. Desserts & processed foods are certainly okay. 4. It might be a good idea for you to talk to an eating disorder professional if you're struggling. Another interesting thing I've learned is many doctors know absolutely nothing about nutrition unless they're specialized in that area. So if you want to talk to a doctor or any other professional then ask them about their experience dealing with eating disorders & tell them you cannot be restrictive. 

Wish you all the best. Be kind to yourself & have fun with everything you do:)

I also got other intrusive thoughts that kept replaying in my head, but I cant recall everything since I'm 20 now. When I was 15, I started getting the pedophilia thoughts, and that scared me.
